intro.summary: A nine-day novena of thanksgiving to God, offering daily prayer and reflection to grow in gratitude for His gifts and providence.

parts.text: In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. O Most Gracious God, Father of all mercies and God of all consolation, I come before You with a heart overflowing with gratitude. You have heard my prayer. You have not abandoned me. In Your infinite goodness, You have poured out upon me blessings I did not deserve and graces I could not have merited. Accept now these nine days of praise and thanksgiving as a small return for Your boundless love. Let my gratitude be not merely of the lips, but of the whole heart, mind, and soul. Especially I give You thanks in this novena for

Amen. Thanksgiving for God’s Faithfulness. “Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; His love endures forever.” Psalm 107:1 Lord God, You are faithful from age to age. When I called, You answered. When I was lost, You found me. When I doubted, You proved Yourself true. Today I give thanks not only for what You have done, but for who You are: unchanging, unshakeable, steadfastly faithful, even when I was not. Intention: I thank You, Lord, for the specific grace and blessing You have granted me. Let this answered prayer deepen my trust in You for all that is yet to come. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen. Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. Holy Saints and Angels, pray for us! Amen. In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Especially I give You thanks in this novena for

Amen. Consecration of Gratitude. “What shall I return to the Lord for all His goodness to me?” Psalm 116, verse 12. Most Blessed Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, I come to the close of these nine days with one desire: that my life itself become a prayer of thanksgiving. Words are not enough. Devotions are not enough. You deserve more than a novena. You deserve all of me. Therefore, Lord, I consecrate to You this answered prayer, these days of gratitude, and my whole life going forward. Use what You have done for me as a witness to Your goodness. Let others see in my life the fruit of a God who hears and answers prayer. I will tell of Your mercies. I will not keep silent. And when the next trial comes, as it surely will, remind me of this day. Let this answered prayer become the stone of remembrance I carry with me into every future uncertainty, that I may say with confidence: He heard me before. He will hear me again. Closing Consecration. Lord my God, I give You thanks with my whole heart. You have answered me. You have been my salvation. Great is Your glory, endless is Your mercy, and faithful is Your love forever. Take now my gratitude, and turn it into praise that never ends, here, and in the life to come. Amen. May the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory, continue to bless you and keep you, now and always. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. Accept now these nine days of praise and thanksgiving as a small return for Your boundless love. Let my gratitude be not merely of the lips, but of the whole heart, mind, and soul. Especially I give You thanks in this novena for  Amen. Thanksgiving for Crosses Carried. “It was good for me to be afflicted, so that I might learn Your decrees.” Psalm 119, verse 71. Gracious God, I thank You even for the trials that preceded this blessing. The waiting, the uncertainty, the nights of doubt, these were not punishments but preparations. You were forming in me a patience and a faith I could not have gained any other way. I now see that even the cross was a gift, shaping me into a vessel fit to receive what You had planned. Intention: Lord, give me the grace to receive future trials with the same trust, knowing that You waste nothing, and that Your purposes are always toward my good and Your glory. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen. Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. Holy Saints and Angels, pray for us. Amen. In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Most Blessed Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, I come to the close of these nine days with one desire: that my life itself become a prayer of thanksgiving. Words are not enough. Devotions are not enough. You deserve more than a novena. You deserve all of me. Therefore, Lord, I consecrate to You this answered prayer, these days of gratitude, and my whole life going forward. Use what You have done for me as a witness to Your goodness. Let others see in my life the fruit of a God who hears and answers prayer. I will tell of Your mercies. I will not keep silent. And when the next trial comes, as it surely will, remind me of this day. Let this answered prayer become the stone of remembrance I carry with me into every future uncertainty, that I may say with confidence: He heard me before. He will hear me again. Closing Consecration. Lord my God, I give You thanks with my whole heart. You have answered me. You have been my salvation. Great is Your glory, endless is Your mercy, and faithful is Your love forever. Take now my gratitude, and turn it into praise that never ends, here, and in the life to come. Amen.
